description: Next external blind compatibility benchmark for KOMPOSOS. Pair identities are separate from audit/blind_test_pairs.json, audit/ground_truth/*.json, audit/external_blind/compatibility_2026_q2.json, and audit/dev_compatibility/*.json.
selection_policy: Thirty-six source-backed pairs selected from external papers, standards, handbooks, and public technical databases. Labels are evidence-backed compatibility outcomes, not outputs from KOMPOSOS. This file must not be used for bridge tuning; misses should define a separate development set before any successor blind benchmark is reported.
holdout_policy: Freeze with SHA256 before first diagnostic run. Do not change scorer logic against this file. If results are inspected, treat this benchmark as spent for future tuning claims and freeze a new blind file for the next publishable external claim.

schema.expected_compatible: true means the pair is reported as usable/stable/standard under the cited context; false means reported incompatibility, decomposition, severe corrosion, immiscibility, or unsuitable direct interface.

pairs.citation: Nitta et al., Materials Today 2015, Li-ion battery materials and current collectors
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum foil is the standard positive-electrode current collector in LiPF6 carbonate Li-ion cells, including LFP cathode coatings.

pairs.citation: Nitta et al., Materials Today 2015, Li-ion battery materials and current collectors
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum foil is used as a positive-electrode current collector for oxide cathodes in passivating LiPF6 electrolytes.

pairs.citation: Li et al., Journal of Power Sources 2007, silicon anode binder and current collector configurations
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper foil is a standard low-potential current collector for composite silicon negative electrodes.

pairs.citation: Zhang, Journal of Power Sources 2006, copper dissolution at high positive potentials in Li-ion batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper current collectors are unsuitable at cathode potentials because copper dissolves under positive-electrode polarization.

pairs.citation: A review of current collectors for lithium-ion batteries, Journal of Power Sources 2021
pairs.evidence_basis: Graphite negative electrodes conventionally use copper collectors; aluminum is not the standard anode collector at low lithiation potentials.

pairs.citation: Mikolajczak et al., Lithium-Ion Batteries Hazard and Use Assessment, Springer 2011, tab and collector materials
pairs.evidence_basis: Nickel tab hardware is common in Li-ion cells and should be scored as a tab connector, not as a full cathode foil.

pairs.citation: Morita et al., Journal of Power Sources 2001, aluminum corrosion in LiTFSI electrolyte
pairs.evidence_basis: LiTFSI electrolytes can corrode aluminum current collectors without protective additives or inhibitors.

pairs.citation: Zhang, Journal of Power Sources 2006, copper dissolution at high positive potentials in Li-ion batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper is not a cathode current collector because it oxidizes and dissolves at positive-electrode potentials.

pairs.citation: Tarascon and Armand, Nature 2001, issues and challenges facing rechargeable lithium batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: PVDF is a standard cathode binder for layered oxide positive electrodes.

pairs.citation: Tarascon and Armand, Nature 2001, issues and challenges facing rechargeable lithium batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: PVDF binder is broadly used in lithium-ion cathode composite electrodes, including lower-voltage LFP systems.

pairs.citation: Bresser et al., Energy & Environmental Science 2018, binder selection by electrode chemistry
pairs.evidence_basis: CMC-type aqueous binders are associated with negative-electrode processing rather than high-voltage cathode binder roles.

pairs.citation: Bresser et al., Energy & Environmental Science 2018, binder selection by electrode chemistry
pairs.evidence_basis: SBR is a common companion binder in aqueous negative-electrode formulations.

pairs.citation: Mindemark et al., Progress in Polymer Science 2018, polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Unprotected PEO electrolyte chemistry has inadequate oxidative stability for high-voltage oxide cathodes.

pairs.citation: Bresser et al., Energy & Environmental Science 2018, binder selection by electrode chemistry
pairs.evidence_basis: CMC/SBR aqueous binder systems are primarily anode binders and are not the default high-voltage NMC cathode binder choice.

pairs.citation: Small things make big deal: powerful binders of lithium batteries and post-lithium batteries, Energy Storage Materials 2019
pairs.evidence_basis: Fluoropolymer binder families are chemically robust cathode binders in lithium battery electrode composites.

pairs.citation: Brydson, Plastics Materials, 8th edition, ABS/PVC blend applications
pairs.evidence_basis: ABS/PVC blends are used commercially for property-balanced thermoplastic compounds.

pairs.citation: MatWeb and commercial wear-grade PPS/PTFE filled compound technical data
pairs.evidence_basis: PTFE-filled high-temperature thermoplastic compounds are used for low-friction PPS-type wear grades.

pairs.citation: ACS Omega 2020, PA6/ABS-compatibilized blends via in situ reactive extrusion
pairs.evidence_basis: PA6/ABS requires reactive compatibilization to overcome immiscibility and poor interfacial adhesion.

pairs.citation: PolymerDatabase.com, polymer blend compatibility and polarity mismatch notes
pairs.evidence_basis: PVC and PA6 have strong polarity, hydrogen-bonding, and processing-window mismatch without a tailored compatibilizer.

pairs.citation: Fluoropolymer surface treatment and adhesive bonding technical literature
pairs.manual_source: Ebnesajjad, Fluoroplastics, Volume 2: Melt Processible Fluoropolymers, William Andrew
pairs.evidence_basis: Untreated PTFE has very low surface energy and is a poor direct adhesive substrate for epoxy bonding.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering; stainless/carbon steel joining guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Austenitic stainless and carbon steel can be mechanically joined or welded with appropriate filler and corrosion design controls.

pairs.citation: ASM Specialty Handbook: Aluminum and Aluminum Alloys, 1993
pairs.evidence_basis: Same-base aluminum alloys are generally compatible for mechanical assemblies with low galvanic mismatch.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, galvanic corrosion of magnesium and aluminum alloys
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Magnesium is highly anodic and has severe galvanic corrosion risk when coupled to more noble aluminum alloys in conductive moisture.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, dissimilar-metal galvanic compatibility guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: High-strength aluminum alloys coupled to passive stainless steel are galvanically risky in conductive wet environments.

pairs.citation: Corrosion Doctors, galvanic corrosion compatibility table
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum/copper direct contact has high galvanic corrosion risk in conductive environments.

pairs.citation: Thevenot, Journal of the European Ceramic Society 1990, boron carbide and silicon carbide ceramics
pairs.evidence_basis: Carbide ceramic families are used in hard composite systems with compatible refractory processing windows.

pairs.citation: Hannink et al., Journal of the American Ceramic Society 2000, transformation toughening in zirconia-containing ceramics
pairs.evidence_basis: Alumina-zirconia composite ceramics are established oxide composite systems.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Ferroelectric oxide and nitride ceramic processing and thermal-expansion constraints make direct composite compatibility poor without engineered interlayers.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Hexagonal boron nitride and silica have dissimilar chemistry, thermal behavior, and bonding requirements for direct dense ceramic integration.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: AlAs and AlGaAs are same-family III-V alloy/barrier materials used in heterostructure design.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: AlN and 4H-SiC are wide-bandgap materials used in nitride/SiC substrate and buffer contexts.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: InAs/InP is a same-family III-V heterostructure pairing used in optoelectronic and quantum-device contexts, usually with strain management.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: II-VI family membership alone does not override wurtzite/zincblende structural and lattice mismatch.

pairs.citation: SCHOTT optical glass data sheets and optical glass catalog
pairs.evidence_basis: BK7-type crown and LAK9-type lanthanum crown optical glasses are catalog optical materials used in cemented or optically contacted assemblies with controlled process conditions.

pairs.citation: Shelby, Introduction to Glass Science and Technology, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Soda-lime glass variants are same-family silicate glasses with broadly similar composition and thermal behavior.

pairs.citation: RP Photonics Encyclopedia, chalcogenide and silica glass fiber material differences
pairs.evidence_basis: Chalcogenide and borosilicate crown glass families have incompatible chemistry and thermal processing windows for direct fusion.
